info.title: Warmbly API
info.description: The Warmbly API lets you drive mailboxes, campaigns, contacts, the unibox, CRM, and more programmatically. Authenticate with an API key as a Bearer token. All paths are relative to the versioned base URL.

post.summary: Link a provider sign-in to an existing password account
post.description: Completes a Google, Apple or OpenID Connect sign-in that came back link_required: the provider's verified address already belongs to an account with a password. A correct password attaches the provider identity to that account and returns the session, or a 2FA challenge when the account has TOTP enrolled (the identity is then attached once /auth/2fa/verify passes). A wrong password is refused like a sign-in and counts against the same per-address budget; three wrong answers, or ten minutes, end the challenge with the code sso_link_expired and the sign-in has to be started again.

400.description: Invalid request body, wrong password (Invalid email or password.), or an unknown, expired, used or exhausted pending token (code sso_link_expired).

403.description: The account or the identity can no longer be linked: the account is suspended, already holds a different identity from this provider, or the identity belongs to another account.

post.description: Changes the signed-in user's password (current + new). Every session the account holds is ended, the calling one included, and the response is the token pair of a new session for the calling device; tokens issued before the change are refused after it. 200.description: Password changed. The body is the token pair of the new session; every earlier token is now refused.

400.description: Invalid request body or weak new password.

409.description: The new password is stored but the calling device could not be issued a new session (code `password_changed_sign_in_again`). Discard the old tokens and sign in again.

post.description: Verifies a TOTP code, enables 2FA, and returns one-time recovery codes (shown once). Requires a user session token (not an API key).

Replaces every recovery code with a fresh set, returned once. Requires a current TOTP or recovery code in the body; a mismatch answers 400 with code two_fa_invalid_code. Requires a user session token (not an API key). Idempotency-Key is not needed: the proof code is single-use, so a retried request is refused rather than rotating the set twice. Wrong codes share the per-account attempt budget with /auth/reauth.

delete.description:
Disconnects and deletes a mailbox. It is removed from all warmup pools, and everything belonging to it goes with it: imported mail, warmup history, credentials, sender links and any scheduled send.

Two parts of the erasure finish just after the response, because neither can be done in the instant the record goes. A Gmail mailbox's OAuth grant is handed back to Google, which invalidates its tokens and removes the app from the customer's third-party access list; Microsoft publishes no per-application revocation endpoint, so an Outlook mailbox's tokens are destroyed locally and the customer removes the app at their Microsoft account. The message bodies stored outside the database are deleted. Both are retried until they succeed.

put.description: Replaces the folders an IMAP mailbox's sync leaves alone. Names are matched as the mail server lists them, without regard to case, and each covers its subfolders. Mail already stored from a newly skipped folder is removed from Warmbly (never from the mailbox), and the mailbox is re-shipped to its worker so the change applies on the next pass. The body is the desired state, so the call is naturally idempotent. INBOX and the sent, drafts, spam, trash and archive folders cannot be skipped.

reopens_at.description: When a mailbox outside its own hours is next open.

health.description: The warmup health band when not healthy.

held.description: A recent spam placement is pausing the climb.

reads_on.description: How the contact reads your mail: each client and device a person's opens came from, most recent first, at most four. Omitted until a person's open says something about itself.

AccountStatusList.description: All of the caller's account statuses under a data envelope (no cursor).

UsageOverview.description: Account, campaign, contact, and API usage counters for the caller.

AuditLog.description: One organization audit-trail entry. actor is null when the acting user has since been deleted; entity_id, changes, and metadata are omitted when empty.

changes.description: Field-level change set; secret values are never recorded.

AuditLogList.description: A page of audit logs with an opaque cursor.

IntegrationCatalogEntry.description: Static metadata for one provider the dashboard renders even when no connection exists.

scopes.description: OAuth scopes requested at authorize time.

events.description: Warmbly events this provider can react to.

action_types.description: Provider action identifiers with a real backend handler.

supports_push.description: Whether this provider can be the target of the synchronous push-contacts action.

capability.description: Configurable-action descriptor the dashboard renders onboarding + field-mapping UI from.

configured.description: Whether the server has OAuth client credentials wired for this provider.

IntegrationConnection.description: One org's link to one provider. Secrets are never serialized.

inbound_webhook_url.description: Returned only at create time for inbound providers (Calendly, Cal.com).

IntegrationConnectionDetail.description: A connection plus its event subscriptions and recent sync runs (the detail drawer payload).

provider.description: A valid api_key/webhook provider id (e.g. close, discord). OAuth providers are rejected.

label.description: Friendly name shown on the connection card.

config.description: Provider-specific config (e.g. the pasted API key or webhook URL).

config_capabilities.description: Per-connection capability snapshot (picker selections, enabled use-cases).

IntegrationEventSubscription.description: Routes a Warmbly event to a provider (or native) action on a connection.

event_type.description: The Warmbly event to react to (e.g. email.replied).

action.description: Provider action id (e.g. slack.notify, hubspot.upsert_contact) or native action (e.g. warmbly.add_tag, warmbly.label_email).

config.description: Action config (e.g. a Slack channel or message template).

use_case.description: Discriminator describing what this automation is for (e.g. crm_sync, notify, custom).

automation_id.description: Set when this subscription is one step of an Automation flow.

event_type.description: The Warmbly event to react to (e.g. email.replied).

config.description: Action config (e.g. a Slack channel or message template).

IntegrationFieldMapping.description: One Warmbly-field to provider-field mapping row.

transform.description: One of '' (none), none, static, uppercase, lowercase, trim.

object.description: The provider object the mappings apply to (e.g. contact).

mappings.description: The full set of mappings to store (replaces any existing).

external_field.description: Destination field on the provider. Required for every mapping.

warmbly_field.description: Source Warmbly field. Required unless transform is 'static'.

transform.description: One of '' (none), none, static, uppercase, lowercase, trim.

IntegrationSyncRun.description: One observability record of work done against a connection.

signing_secret.description: HMAC signing secret used to verify outbound webhook signatures.

contact_ids.description: Contact ids to push. Deduplicated server-side. At least 1, at most 500. Required unless all is set.

all.description: Resolve the selection from filters instead of contacts.

filters.description: The search whose matches the action applies to. Required when all is true.

exclude.description: Contact ids to drop from the resolved set. Ignored unless all is set.

IntegrationPushRequest.description: Contacts to push. The resolved set is capped at 500 whichever form is used: the push calls the CRM once per contact inside the request.

MeetingBooking.description: One booked meeting from a connected scheduling provider (Calendly, Cal.com) or a manually logged meeting.

Automation.description: A branching flow: when the trigger event fires, the executor walks the graph, evaluating condition nodes and running the action nodes on matched paths.

trigger_event.description: The event that fires the flow (e.g. email.replied).

filter.description: Optional automation-wide gate (e.g. intents / min_confidence) applied to every action.

AutomationWrite.description: Create/update payload from the flow builder.

enabled.description: Whether the automation runs on matching events.

trigger_event.description: The event that fires the flow (e.g. email.replied).

filter.description: Optional automation-wide gate applied to every action.

AutomationGraph.description: The editable flow: nodes plus the edges connecting them.

id.description: Node id. The single trigger node uses id 'trigger'.

type.description: Exactly one trigger node; condition nodes have true/false outgoing edges; action nodes run a handler.

action.description: Action node only: provider action (e.g. slack.notify) or native action (e.g. warmbly.add_tag, warmbly.label_email, warmbly.run_automation).

connection_id.description: Action node only: the integration connection the action runs against. Omitted for native (warmbly.*) actions.

when.description: '' for plain edges; 'true' / 'false' for the two outgoing edges of a condition node.

AutomationCondition.description: An IF test evaluated against the trigger event's data.

key.description: For 'field' conditions, the event-data key to test.

expression.description: For 'expression' conditions, a Go-template predicate evaluated against the event data.

AutomationDryRunRequest.description: Optional. When omitted, the server builds a sample event from the trigger.

data.description: Sample event payload to evaluate the flow against.
The resolved event data the flow was evaluated against.

AutomationRun.description: One execution of an automation graph (per fired event or manual launch).

AutomationNodeResult.description: One node's outcome in a run (or a dry-run trace).

preview.description: Dry-run only: what the action would send.

Team.description: A named, color-tagged grouping of an organization's members.

color.description: Hex color for the chip (defaults to #94a3b8).

members.description: The members that belong to this team. Always an array (never null).

TeamMember.description: One membership row of a team, with the user's email and name joined for display.

TeamCollection.description: A bare collection of teams (not cursor-paginated).

TeamCreate.description: Request body for creating a team.

TeamUpdate.description: Partial-update body for a team. Omitted fields are left untouched.

TeamAddMember.description: Request body for adding an existing organization member to a team.

user_id.description: The member's user id (must already belong to the organization).

monthly_credits.description: AI writing-assistant monthly credit grant for this plan.

PlanList.description: The list of public subscription plans.

TimezoneOption.description: A supported timezone identifier and its display label.

recipient_email.description: The recipient address the event is about.

campaign_id.description: Campaign the event is attributed to.

task_id.description: Send task the event is attributed to.

contact_id.description: Contact the event is attributed to.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON attached to the event.

TaskDeadLetter.description: A task that exhausted its retry budget and landed in the dead-letter queue.

id.description: Dead-letter record ID (use this to replay).

TaskDeadLetterList.description: List of dead-letter records. Not cursor-paginated.

WarmupRoutingRule.description: A customer-defined preference applied during premium-pool partner selection.

sender_match_value.description: Lowercased/trimmed; empty when sender_match_type is any.

recipient_match_value.description: Lowercased/trimmed; empty when recipient_match_type is any.

weight.description: Selection weight, >= 0. Exactly 0 excludes the pairing outright.

WarmupRoutingRuleInput.description: Create/update payload for a warmup routing rule. A match value is required unless its match type is `any`.

priority.description: Evaluation order, ascending. Lower runs first.

sender_match_value.description: Required unless sender_match_type is any. Domain (acme.com), TLD (com), or provider bucket (google, microsoft, yahoo, apple, proton, zoho, custom).

recipient_match_value.description: Required unless recipient_match_type is any. Same value forms as the sender side.

weight.description: Selection weight, must be >= 0. Above 1 prefers the pairing, below 1 avoids it, and exactly 0 excludes it even when no other partner is available.

WarmupRoutingRuleList.description: Warmup routing rules under a `rules` key (always an array, never null). Not cursor-paginated.

user_id.description: Owner (the user that created the template).

ReplyTemplateList.description: Reply templates under a `data` key. Not cursor-paginated.

UpdateReplyTemplate.description: All fields optional; omitted fields are left unchanged.

ids.description: Template IDs in their new order (1-indexed). IDs omitted are left untouched.

ScoreTemplateRequest.description: Content to score. body_plain is preferred over body_html when present.

TemplateScoreSpan.description: One exact fragment of the copy that triggered an issue.

text.description: The fragment as it is written in the copy.

excerpt.description: The whole line, for context around the fragment.

field.description: Set when the issue lives in exactly one half of the template. Absent when it straddles both or describes the send as a whole.

spans.description: The exact fragments that caused the issue, in reading order. Capped at 8; the count that drives the deduction is taken before the cap.

SpamFinding.description: One located problem the AI analysis found. `text` is verified against the submitted copy before it is returned, so it is never a fragment the caller did not send.

field.description: Absent when the model labelled neither half and nothing in the finding could be anchored in the copy.

text.description: The fragment quoted from the copy. Absent when the finding is about the email as a whole.

issue.description: Why this fragment hurts deliverability or replies.

TemplateAnalysis.description: AI spam analysis of a campaign template, with the rules-based pass alongside it.

score.description: Overall deliverability score (higher is safer), grounded on the rules pass.

verdict.description: One sentence on how the email will land.

suggested_subject.description: A rewritten subject, absent when the current one is fine.

improvements.description: Copy-level advice with no single fragment to quote.

SuppressedRecipient.description: One entry on the workspace suppression list. A domain entry keeps the bare host in `email` and matches every address at it.

email.description: The address, or the bare domain when kind is domain.

value.description: An address, or a bare domain (with or without a leading @).

reason.description: Applied to every entry without its own reason.

skipped.description: Values that were neither a valid address nor a valid domain.

ContactLinkClick.description: The link behind an email_clicked event: where it went, the anchor text it was minted from, and the UTM parameters the destination carried.

label.description: Anchor text the link was minted from.

EngagementOrigin.description: Where an open or click came from. Every field is omitted when unknown; the source address itself is never stored.

client.description: Mail client named by the user agent, for example Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail, Thunderbird. On a click, the app whose in-app browser opened the link, when it says so.

client_type.description: Whether the open came from an installed mail app or webmail in a browser. Omitted when the request cannot tell. On a click it is `app` only when a mail app made the request itself, and never `webmail`.

device_hidden.description: True when a mailbox provider's image proxy fetched the image (Gmail, Yahoo, Apple Mail Privacy Protection), so the reader's device is unknowable. device_type, os and browser are then omitted, and so is the location for proxies that do not keep the reader's region.

ContactReadingOrigin.description: One client and device a contact opened mail on.

opens.description: A person's opens from this client and device.

WebsitePageHit.description: A page view reported by the website tracking snippet and tied to the contact through an email-link ticket.

landing.description: True for the first view of a session.

Label.description: One entry in a workspace label registry (a folder, tag or category). Registries belong to the organization, so every member sees and can edit the same set.

color.description: Hex colour, `#rrggbb`. Omit to let the server pick from its palette.

LabelOrder.description: One label's place in the registry after a move.

CampaignLeadHold.description: One contact's flow parked inside one campaign.

until.description: When it lifts. Absent for a hold with no end, which only a resume lifts.

reason.description: Free-text note shown next to the hold.

hold.description: Absent when the lead is not held, including a dated hold that has expired.

until.description: When the hold lifts. Must be in the future and within a year. Omit or null for a hold with no end.

reason.description: Optional note shown next to the hold.

is_default.description: The identity the provider composes from by default. Reported, not followed: which alias Warmbly sends from is the workspace's own choice.

verified.description: The provider finished verifying the address. An unverified one is listed but cannot be selected.

supported.description: False for Outlook and SMTP/IMAP mailboxes, which publish no send-as list.

mailbox_email.description: The address the mailbox authenticates as, which is always a legal sender.

send_as_email.description: The alias in use. Empty means the mailbox address.

synced_at.description: When the list was last read from the provider.

signature_source.description: Where the mailbox's stored signature came from.

import_signature.description: Also replace the mailbox's stored signature with the one configured at the provider, for whichever identity the mailbox sends as. An empty signature at the provider changes nothing.

TaskSelection.description: Names the tasks a bulk action applies to: either an explicit id list, or every task matching a search (all + filters) minus the ids in exclude. The filter form lets one call cover far more tasks than a page, and is refused with selection_too_large past 50000 matches.

tasks.description: Task ids (1 to 1000). Required unless all is set.

all.description: Resolve the selection from filters instead of tasks.

filters.description: The search whose matches the action applies to. Required when all is true.

exclude.description: Task ids to drop from the resolved set. Ignored unless all is set.

BulkUpdateTasks.description: A task selection plus the fields to write on every task in it. At least one of status or priority is required.

status.description: Status to set. completed stamps completed_at and records the completion on each linked contact's timeline.

BulkTasksResponse.description: How many tasks the bulk action touched. The count is returned rather than the rows: a select-all can cover tens of thousands.

MailboxImportSettings.description: Applied to every mailbox an import connects or updates; a mapped column overrides them per row. Omitted fields leave the mailbox as it is.

shared_password.description: Used for rows with no password of their own.

on_existing.description: What happens to an address already in the workspace. Default update.

tracking_domains.description: Tracking host per sending domain, such as {"acme.io": "track.acme.io"}. Up to 500 domains.

redirects.description: Root redirect per sending domain, such as {"acme.io": "https://acme.com"}. Uses the inbox vendor's forwarding when a connected vendor account holds the domain. Up to 500 domains.

MailboxImportForm.description: A file or pasted text, plus the mapping and options as JSON strings.

file.description: CSV, TSV or XLSX, up to 10 MB.

text.description: A pasted list, used when no file is sent.

mapping.description: JSON object of column index to field, such as {"0":"email","1":"password"}. Omit for the automatic mapping.

MailboxImportPreview.description: What an import of this input would do, row by row and domain by domain.

vendor.description: A recognised export, when one is.

source.description: Where the rows came from: a file, a pasted list, an inbox vendor, or an admin grant (workspace).

fields.description: The uploaded cells that are not passwords.

MailboxImportRowFix.description: Corrects one failed row; omitted fields keep what was uploaded.

MailboxImportRetry.description: Requeues failed rows: all of them (empty body), those with one cause, or the listed lines.

password.description: One new password for every requeued row.

VendorConnection.description: An inbox vendor account. Its key never leaves the server.

vendor.description: A vendor id from the catalog. Ignored on update.

fields.description: The vendor's fields, keyed as the catalog lists them.

MailboxSourceImportRequest.description: Which vendor mailboxes or directory users to import, plus the same options as a file import.

all.description: Every mailbox or enabled user not yet in the workspace.

DomainGrant.description: An administrator's grant over a Google Workspace domain or a Microsoft 365 organization. Holds no token.

tenant.description: The Workspace domain, or the Microsoft tenant id.

admin_email.description: Google only: the super administrator the directory is read as.

google_client_id.description: The service account client id a Workspace administrator authorizes.

google_missing.description: Instance settings still unset for Google grants; empty when ready.

microsoft_missing.description: Instance settings still unset for Microsoft grants; empty when ready.

GoogleGrantStart.description: How the workspace proves it controls the Workspace domain.

url.description: The Google sign-in for the administrator (method signin).

txt_value.description: warmbly-verify=<value>, unique to the workspace and domain. Always present: the DNS proof works either way.

GoogleGrantFinish.description: Either state and code from the Google sign-in, or domain and admin_email once the TXT record is published.

id.description: The address (Google) or Graph user id (Microsoft).

upgrade.description: The user's mailbox is already in the workspace on its own sign-in with the same provider (not held by Warmbly Cloud). Connecting it moves that mailbox onto the grant in place, keeping its history, campaigns and warmup; all: true includes it.

VendorDomainLink.description: A sending domain held by a connected inbox vendor account, with what its API can do for it.

forwarding.description: The current forwarding target, when the vendor reports it.

can_unforward.description: Whether an empty url removes the forwarding.

forwarding_reviewed.description: A forwarding change is a request the vendor's staff apply later.

vendors.description: The inbox vendors this domain's mailboxes were imported from.

mailboxes.description: How many mailboxes on the domain were changed.

kind.description: workspace moves onto an admin grant; personal is a shared address such as gmail.com and moves to an app password.

grant_id.description: The workspace's active Google grant covering the domain, when there is one.
